cover.headline: The rupee, Lannett and Pen-G lift FY27; the US base is flat and Eugia is stuck behind the FDA. At 18x, the price is about right
cover.lead: Aurobindo is India's largest generics exporter to the US by approved products (737 final approvals) and a top-ten generics company in eight European countries. FY26 revenue was ₹33,653 cr: US 43%, Europe 31%, APIs 12%, Growth Markets 10%, ARV 4%. Q1FY27 revenue rose 16.3% and operating EBITDA +20% to ₹1,924 cr (21.0% margin), but about two-thirds of the revenue growth was the weaker rupee (₹94.5 vs ₹85.5 per dollar); US sales in dollars were $399mn, below the $426mn of two years earlier. The stock has risen {{P.returns.1y|chg}} in a year to ₹1,672: 21.7x our FY27E EPS and 19.0x FY28E. The street values Aurobindo on **P/E on FY28E or 12-month-forward EPS (18-20x)**. We forecast EPS of ₹77.1 / 87.9 / 96.4 for FY27-29E (per post-buyback share), in line with PL and Motilal Oswal and far below ICICI Direct. Applying **18x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹92.1** (Aurobindo's own forward median on EPS before exceptional items, 17.1x, re-rated by the pharma sector's +5.45%) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,549, DCF ₹1,281. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: FY27 growth is mostly the rupee and Lannett
arguments.p: Of our 16.7% FY27E revenue growth, ~6.2 points are currency and ~5.5 points Lannett (the US generics maker bought for $250mn, closed 29-Jun-2026); organic growth is ~5.0%. US revenue fell 7% in dollars in FY26 as generic Revlimid faded; ex-Revlimid it grew 5% quarter on quarter in Q1. Lannett adds ~$60mn a quarter, a US plant at 40% utilisation and a generic Advair launch.

arguments.h: Europe and the API backbone are the real improvement
arguments.p: Europe passed EUR1bn in FY26 and grew 11% in constant currency in Q1 (EUR267mn) with EBITDA margins now above 20%, up from single digits four years ago, as products move to Aurobindo's own plants in India and China. The Pen-G plant (₹3,058 cr) now supplies the company's penicillins, with PLI support and a minimum import price to Jan-2027. Gross margin reached 61.3% in Q4FY26.

arguments.h: Injectables are stuck behind the FDA
arguments.p: Eugia, the ~$500mn injectables arm, has Unit III under a warning letter since Aug-2024 and re-classified OAI in 2026, and Unit I received a warning letter on 13-Aug-2026. Management guides single-digit growth. Biosimilars (four EU/UK approvals, US filings due) and the MSD biologics contract plant are options that pay mostly after FY28.

At 19.0x FY28E Aurobindo trades above its 17.1x forward median since 2021 (on EPS before exceptional items), after a 53% rally. Our 18x target multiple equals ICICI Direct's and PL's. ROE is ~11% against an 11.9% cost of equity and the DCF (₹1,281) sits below the price: the bull case needs the US base and Eugia to grow again.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with Lannett and generic Advair; whether EBITDA reaches the ~₹2,200 cr a quarter management is aiming for.
Eugia: the response to the Unit I warning letter (13-Aug-2026) and the Unit III remediation; any FDA re-inspection.
Biosimilars: EMA filing of omalizumab (due Q3 2026) and the first US filings (omalizumab, denosumab, bevacizumab) promised for 2026.
US trade policy: the 21-Jul-2026 proposal of a 100% tariff on imported generics from 2028 unless made in the US; Lannett is Aurobindo's hedge.
Pen-G: renewal or lapse of the minimum import price (expires Jan-2027) and the FY26 PLI payment; TheraNym Unit 1 qualification from Nov-2026.

sections.title: What Aurobindo does: a high-volume generics maker for the US and Europe, built on its own APIs

blocks.p: Aurobindo makes generic (off-patent) medicines and the active ingredients (APIs) that go into them, in 30+ plants, mostly around Hyderabad. It has five businesses. **US formulations** (₹14,408 cr in FY26, 42.8% of revenue; $1631mn) sells tablets, capsules, injectables and specialty products to US wholesalers and pharmacy chains; it has 737 approved generic applications (ANDAs), more than any other Indian company, and launches ~10 products a quarter. The injectables and specialty part sits in Eugia (~$513mn in FY26, ~70% in the US). **Europe** (₹10,315 cr, 30.7%; EUR1006mn) sells generics in the UK, Germany, France, Spain, Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and other countries, through businesses bought from Actavis, Apotex and Generis. **Growth Markets** (₹3,499 cr, 10.4%) covers Canada, Brazil, South Africa, Indonesia, China and, since 2022, India. **ARV** (₹1,384 cr, 4.1%) sells HIV medicines to donor-funded programmes. **APIs** (₹4,047 cr, 12%) sells ingredients to other drug makers, led by penicillins and cephalosporins (beta-lactams), where it is one of the world's largest producers.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Aurobindo is a scale-and-cost business, not a franchise business. It wins by making a very wide range of medicines cheaply from its own ingredients and supplying them reliably. That protects volumes but not prices: in the US, the products it sells today lose value every year and must be replaced by new launches. Earnings therefore track three things: launch flow, plant compliance and costs.

sections.title: Industry: US generics pay for volume and cost; Europe for reliability; tariffs are the new wild card

blocks.p: **United States.** The US is the largest generics market and the hardest. Three wholesaler-led buying groups buy most generics, so prices fall every year on old products (mid-single digits is the industry norm) and a new generic loses most of its price within months once several rivals enter. Money is made on volume, on cost (backward-integrated APIs) and on products that few can copy: injectables, controlled substances, inhalers, complex topicals. Plant compliance is the gate: a warning letter or OAI stops new approvals from a site.

**Tariffs.** On 2-Apr-2026 the US imposed a 100% Section 232 tariff on patented medicines; generics and their ingredients were exempted 'at this time' (effective 31-Jul-2026 for listed firms, 29-Sep-2026 for others). On 21-Jul-2026 President Trump said imported generics would stay tariff-free for about two years, then face 100% from Aug-2028 and 200% from 2029 unless makers build US plants (a social-media post, not yet law). About 90% of India's pharma exports to the US are generics (GTRI, Sep-2026).

**Europe.** European generics are bought through national tenders and price-controlled pharmacy markets: low prices but stable volumes and few US-style collapses. Scale, a broad portfolio and reliable supply win; Aurobindo is among the top ten generic companies in eight European countries and passed EUR1bn of sales in FY26 after a decade of acquisitions (Actavis, Generis, Apotex).

**Growth Markets, ARV and APIs.** Growth Markets (Canada, Brazil, South Africa, Indonesia, China, India and others) are smaller, branded or semi-branded and grow faster; Aurobindo entered India's branded market only in 2022 (Veritaz) and added GLS and the Khandelwal brands. ARV formulations are anti-HIV medicines sold mostly through donor-funded tenders (PEPFAR, Global Fund); volumes are large, prices are set by tender and margins thin; donor funding cuts are a risk. India still imports most penicillin intermediates from China. The government's PLI scheme pays ₹240 cr per 10,000 t of Pen-G produced, and from 29-Jan-2026 a one-year minimum import price applies to Pen-G (₹2,216/kg), amoxicillin (₹2,733/kg) and 6-APA (₹3,405/kg).

**Biosimilars.** Biosimilars (copies of biologic drugs) need large plants and clinical trials (~US$450mn invested by Aurobindo since 2018). Europe buys oncology biosimilars through tenders with 10+ players per molecule and 75-85% price erosion (CEO); regulators in Europe and the US are starting to waive phase-3 efficacy studies, which lowers the entry cost for everyone.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the tailwinds that reach Aurobindo are mostly on the cost side (own APIs, China plant, supply security) and the currency. The ones investors pay up for in Indian pharma (domestic branded growth, specialty products, US price discipline) mostly do not. That is why Aurobindo has traded at a discount to the sector for a decade, and why we do not add a premium.

sections.title: US: a ~$400mn-a-quarter base that is not growing; Lannett adds a plant and ~$240mn

blocks.p: Aurobindo sells ~$1.6bn a year of generics in the US: tablets and capsules made mainly at Units III, VII and APL Healthcare in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, plus injectables (Eugia, next chapter) and specialty products. It has 737 final ANDA approvals, 33 tentative and 126 under review (Jun-2026) and launched 10 products in Q1FY27. The business in dollars has gone nowhere: $1,750mn in FY25, $1631mn in FY26 (−7%), $399mn in Q1FY27 vs $426mn in Q1FY25. Part of that is generic Revlimid (lenalidomide), sold under volume limits and never disclosed separately; excluding it, group revenue grew 9.5% in FY26 and US sales rose from $381mn (Q4FY26) to $399mn (Q1FY27). The rest is the usual US arithmetic: ~10 launches a quarter roughly offset price erosion on the existing portfolio. The US CEO agreed that ~$400mn a quarter is the base.

blocks.h: Tariffs: a risk Aurobindo is better placed for than most

blocks.p: On 2-Apr-2026 the US imposed a 100% Section 232 tariff on patented medicines; generics and their ingredients were exempted 'at this time' (effective 31-Jul-2026 for listed firms, 29-Sep-2026 for others). On 21-Jul-2026 President Trump said imported generics would stay tariff-free for about two years, then face 100% from Aug-2028 and 200% from 2029 unless makers build US plants (a social-media post, not yet law). About 90% of India's pharma exports to the US are generics (GTRI, Sep-2026). Aurobindo is the most US-exposed large Indian generics maker by volume, so a tariff would hurt it most; but it is also one of the few with US plants (Lannett, AuroLife, Dayton, Raleigh). The US CEO's view is that a blanket rule would be "a level playing ground": prices would have to rise for everyone. We assume no tariff in our forecasts (they end in FY29) and treat it as a bear-case risk.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model US revenue of $1800 / 1940 / 2000mn for FY27-29E: a base of $1605 / 1650 / 1685mn (flat to +2.5% a year in dollars, as launches offset price erosion and Eugia cannot launch from its blocked sites) plus Lannett at $195 / 290 / 315mn. That is close to management's $2bn by FY29E but gets there by acquisition, not organic growth. At FY27E rates the US is 43.3% of revenue. Every $50mn of US revenue is ~₹480 cr of revenue and, at ~30% incremental margin, ~₹145 cr of EBITDA (~2% of FY28E EPS).

sections.title: Injectables: a $500mn business with two warning letters; growth is on hold

blocks.p: Eugia Pharma Specialities makes Aurobindo's injectables (sterile medicines given by drip or syringe), oncology and hormone products and penems in five sites near Hyderabad, plus a US unit. Global specialty and injectables revenue was $513mn in FY26, ~$480mn excluding generic Revlimid, ~70% of it in the US. Injectables are the most attractive part of US generics: hard to make, often in shortage, fewer competitors. But the FDA has blocked new approvals from the two sites that matter most. Unit III (injectables and ophthalmics, 149 ANDAs) has been under a warning letter since Aug-2024; it was re-inspected in Jan-Feb 2026 (11 observations, which management called "procedural") and classified OAI again. Unit I (oncology and hormones, 61 ANDAs) was inspected in Feb-2026, classified OAI and received a warning letter dated 13-Aug-2026 that criticises its aseptic processing and calls Units II and III "unacceptable" too. Management now guides single-digit growth and ~$500mn+ of revenue for FY27.

bullets: **What a warning letter does:** existing products keep shipping (the company says there is no impact on current US supplies), but the FDA can withhold approval of new products made at the site until it re-inspects and is satisfied. That can take years: Unit III has been under a warning letter since Aug-2024.

**How much is at stake:** Unit I is ~2% of group revenue (company); Unit III holds 108 of Eugia's 167 approved US products. The bigger cost is the launches that cannot happen: 59 pending applications.

**History repeats:** Unit III's 2024 warning letter followed data-integrity findings; the 2026 Unit I letter cites repeat aseptic-processing failures across Eugia. This is the main compliance risk in the group.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we assume Eugia grows ~5% a year in dollars and that no blocked site is cleared before FY28; we do not cut existing supplies. A clean re-inspection of Unit III would add ~$50-100mn of US revenue over two years (our bull case); an import alert at either site (not our base case) would remove existing sales and is the single biggest downside risk in the US.

sections.title: Europe: EUR1bn, growing ~10% a year, margin now above 20%

blocks.p: Europe is the part of Aurobindo that has improved most. Built from Actavis's Western European businesses (2014), Generis in Portugal (2017) and Apotex's businesses in five countries (2019), it passed EUR1bn of sales in FY26 (EUR1006mn, +9% in euros) and grew 11% in constant currency in Q1FY27 to EUR267mn. Management says its EBITDA margin has risen from single digits three to four years ago to above 20%, by replacing third-party suppliers with Aurobindo's own plants in India and, increasingly, China (10+ products already transferred) and by cutting costs. Europe is also the first market for Aurobindo's biosimilars, sold directly and through STADA and Orion. Antibiotics, a large part of the basket, sell more in the autumn-winter flu season.

blocks.h: The Pen-G plant: India's bet on penicillin self-reliance

blocks.p: Aurobindo spent ₹3,058 cr on a fermentation plant at Kakinada (Lyfius Pharma, with 6-APA at Qule Pharma) to make Penicillin-G and 6-APA, the starting materials for amoxicillin and other penicillins that India imported almost entirely from China. It runs under the government's PLI scheme, which pays ₹240 cr for every 10,000 t produced, on 15,000 t of capacity. After a slow start (42% average utilisation in FY25, an EBITDA loss of ₹200 cr+ in FY26) output reached ~11,300 t annualised in March-2026 and 800-900 t a month since; the business turned EBITDA positive in Q4FY26 and gross margin rose as Aurobindo stopped importing. On 29-Jan-2026 India set a one-year minimum import price on Pen-G (₹2,216/kg), amoxicillin and 6-APA, and imports have dropped. Management says it aims to be profitable "irrespective of the MIP or PLI".

sections.title: Biosimilars and the MSD plant: real progress, small revenue before FY29

blocks.p: **Biosimilars (CuraTeQ).** Aurobindo has invested ~US$450mn since 2018 (capex and R&D). Approved: Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim: EMA, MHRA, Health Canada), Zefylti (filgrastim: EMA, MHRA), Bevqolva (bevacizumab: MHRA, Health Canada, CDSCO), Dazublys (trastuzumab: EMA, MHRA, CDSCO); all four now supplied commercially in the UK; rollout in seven EU countries; tenders in Mexico. Filed: Denosumab (Filvizy / Fugevy) with EMA and CDSCO; omalizumab EMA filing due Q3 2026; first US filings (omalizumab, denosumab, bevacizumab) 'imminent'. Later: Tocilizumab (filing 2027), ranibizumab (phase 3), trastuzumab SC (phase 1 in 2026), next wave of eight products (2030+). Partners: STADA (two EMA-approved biosimilars, France/Germany), Orion (Nordics), partners in Algeria, Uzbekistan, Mexico. Guidance: 7-8 products in EU, UK and Canada by 2028-29; at least three in the US by 2030; gross margin ~65% after price erosion. The CEO describes the start as "modest, steady and measured": European oncology biosimilars are sold through tenders with 10-11 competitors, so Aurobindo aims for small shares at low cost rather than 15-20% of a market; omalizumab (a ~$4bn molecule with three serious rivals) is the first product where it expects to be in the first wave.

**Biologics contract manufacturing (TheraNym).** Biologics contract manufacturer (CMO) anchored by Merck Sharp & Dohme: first product schedule signed 29-May-2024, second in FY26, third (Unit 2) in Apr-2026. Unit 1 (60 kL) inaugurated 3-Jun-2026, qualification from Nov-2026, validation batches in 2027, steady revenue from calendar 2028. Unit 2 (60 kL drug substance, US$150-180mn capex) construction from Oct-2026, revenue from 2031. Target US$150-200mn of revenue from 2032 at 35-50% EBITDA margin.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Aurobindo has a cost moat, not a franchise. Its breadth (700+ approved US products, 4,000+ European registrations) and its own APIs, now including penicillin starting materials, let it supply cheaply and reliably, which keeps it in the top tier of generics suppliers. But it has no brands that doctors ask for, no meaningful Indian business and no product that holds its price for long. Returns (ROE ~10-11%) show it: the advantage protects volumes, not margins. If the biosimilar and contract-manufacturing bets work, that could change after FY29.

sections.title: Revenue up 8% a year since FY19; EPS only 6%, with a deep dip in FY23

blocks.p: Aurobindo's revenue grew from ₹19,564 cr in FY19 to ₹33,653 cr in FY26 (8% a year), as Europe was built by acquisition, injectables grew and the US kept adding products. Profit grew more slowly. EPS before exceptional items went from ₹41.5 to ₹61.3 (6% a year): margins fell from 21% to 15% in FY23, when US prices collapsed, Eugia's injectable plants ran into FDA trouble and raw-material costs spiked, and depreciation nearly doubled from FY20 as the company built new plants. FY21's reported EPS of ₹91 is inflated by the ₹2,815 cr gain on selling Natrol, its US vitamins business. In FY24-25 a generic version of Revlimid (lenalidomide), sold under volume limits, helped US profits; it faded through FY26, when reported revenue grew 6% but 9.5% excluding it.

blocks.p: Gross margin (revenue less materials) rose from 58.8% in Q1FY26 to 61.3% in Q4FY26 and 60.4% in Q1FY27, its best levels in five years: the company now makes its own penicillin intermediates (Pen-G and 6-APA) instead of importing them from China, ships more of Europe's products from its own plants in India and China, and sells more injectables. But employee cost rose from 14.2% of revenue (Q1FY25) to 16.2% (Q1FY27) as new plants were staffed (Pen-G, China, biosimilars, US sites), and the Pen-G plant uses a lot of power. The result is an EBITDA margin that has sat at 20-21% for nine quarters.

sections.title: Earnings quality: reasonable, but exceptional items, other income and capitalised R&D need watching

bullets: **Exceptional items recur.** FY21: gain on sale of natrol (us nutraceuticals) (₹2,815 cr); FY22: impairments and other one-offs (₹-139 cr); FY24: impairment (q4fy24) (₹-168 cr); FY26: new labour codes (gratuity past service cost), q3fy26 (₹-65 cr); Q1FY27: exceptional item (rs40 cr) plus a rs43 cr loss on derecognising the east windsor lease receivable inside ebitda (₹-83 cr). FY21's Natrol gain is large enough to distort the reported P/E history (and its trough test), so we value on EPS before exceptional items (see Valuation).

**Other income is partly one-off.** FY26 other income was ₹492 cr (~10% of pre-tax profit): ₹305 cr of treasury income (3.2% on ~₹9,500 cr of average gross cash), ₹27 cr of interest on a US sub-lease receivable that has now been written off, ₹155 cr of unexplained "miscellaneous income" and small write-backs. FY25 included a ₹120.5 cr gain on that sub-lease. Q1FY27 other income doubled to ₹212 cr without explanation. Screener adds forex gains and nets exceptional items, so its figures differ.

**Some development spend is capitalised.** Intangible assets under development rose from ₹1,634 cr to ₹2,205 cr in FY26 (product filings, biosimilars), on top of ₹1,590 cr of R&D expensed (4.7% of revenue). Capitalised development flatters EBITDA today and adds amortisation and impairment risk later.

**Cash conversion is weak.** Operating cash flow was 42%, 60% and 80% of EBITDA in FY24-26 (Screener); inventory was 326 days of material cost in FY26. Free cash flow after capex was ₹2,421 cr in FY26 and negative in FY24.
**High tax rate.** 31.5% in FY26 and 31.9% in Q1FY27, because losses in new subsidiaries (CuraTeQ, TheraNym, China) get no tax credit. It should fall as they turn profitable (guided 28-29%).
**Small minorities and JV.** Minorities absorbed a ₹2 cr loss in FY26; we use profit attributable to owners (patch to Screener's net-profit row). Equity-accounted JVs are immaterial.

**Audit and disclosures.** Deloitte Haskins & Sells (appointed Aug-2022 for five years); unmodified opinion for FY26. Revenue by business is disclosed every quarter; EBITDA by business is not (except management comments). Contingent liabilities (mainly tax) were ₹682 cr at Mar-2026 (~₹12 a share).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing alarming, but several items move reported EPS by 1-5% in a typical year (exceptional items, the sub-lease gain and write-off, forex, unexplained other income), development spend is increasingly capitalised, and working capital absorbs a large part of profit. We forecast no exceptional items and no forex gains.

blocks.p: Aurobindo runs gross cash and gross debt side by side: at Jun-2026 it held ₹8,790 cr of cash and investments and ₹8,393 cr of debt, mostly foreign-currency working-capital and term loans (₹6,709 cr of ₹7,673 cr at Mar-2026; packing credit at 2.2-4.4%), so net cash was only ₹397 cr (US$42mn) after paying for Lannett (US$247mn) and the buyback (US$85mn). The average cost of debt was 4.8% in Q1FY27. The real drag is working capital: inventory was ₹12,053 cr at Mar-2026, 326 days of material cost (Screener), as the company stocks thousands of products for many markets and builds inventory for launches; receivables rose to 77 days.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
Meaning
rows: Penicillin-G and 6-aminopenicillanic acid: fermentation-made starting materials for amoxicillin and other penicillins.
Abbreviated New Drug Application: the US filing to sell a generic. "Tentative approval" means approved but blocked by patents or exclusivity.
Active pharmaceutical ingredient: the drug substance itself, sold to other formulators.
Anti-retroviral (HIV) medicines, mostly sold to donor-funded programmes through tenders.
The penicillin and cephalosporin family of antibiotics; made in segregated plants.
A near-copy of a biologic medicine (an antibody or protein made in living cells), approved on comparative data.
Contract (development and) manufacturing organisation: makes medicines for other companies (TheraNym for MSD).
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; here the company definition, before forex and other income.
Enterprise value (market value plus debt minus cash) divided by EBITDA.
One-off gains or losses shown separately (FY21 Natrol gain, impairments, the FY26 labour-code charge). Our valuation history uses EPS before them.
US FDA inspection observations / Official Action Indicated (serious findings) / a formal letter after which the FDA can withhold new approvals from the site.
Share price divided by the next full fiscal year's EPS.
Generic lenalidomide (Revlimid, a blood-cancer drug), sold in the US under volume-limited settlements until early 2026; a temporary, high-margin product.
Revenue less cost of materials, as % of revenue.
Minimum import price: imports below it are restricted (Pen-G, 6-APA, amoxicillin, from 29-Jan-2026 for one year).
Oral solid dosage: tablets and capsules.
Production-Linked Incentive: a government subsidy tied to output (₹240 cr per 10,000 t of Pen-G).
The annual fall in the price of a generic as more competitors enter and buyers renegotiate.
Return on equity (profit ÷ shareholders' funds) / return on capital employed (operating profit ÷ debt plus equity).
The median of pharma peers' P/E at 30-Sep-2026 vs their five-year medians (+5.45% excluding Aurobindo), applied to Aurobindo's own historical multiple.
Half of FY28E EPS plus half of FY29E EPS: the twelve-month-forward EPS the market will look at in September 2027, when the target falls due.
House rule: a forward year whose EPS is a loss or below half the highest EPS of the previous three years is left out of the P/E median.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Aurobindo Pharma (consolidated, Rs crore; profit attributable to owners, see tools/authoring/AUROPHARMA.patch.js). Aurobindo reports one segment and revenue by business (US, Europe, Growth Markets, ARV formulations; APIs), so the engine runs on one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the business-line build (US and Growth Markets/ARV in US dollars, Europe in euros, each times an assumed rate; APIs in rupees) sits in `businessLines` and AUROPHARMA.ctx.js checks that it equals model revenue. Engine workarounds: (1) the Lannett acquisition (US$247mn paid in Q1FY27, Rs2,335 cr) and A1 Biochem (US$13.6mn) are carried in FY27E capex because the engine has no acquisitions line (Lannett's price buys a plant, products and working capital that are depreciated/amortised like capex); (2) the Rs800 cr buyback of Apr-May 2026 is carried in the FY27E payout (no buyback line) and the per-share target uses the post-buyback count of 57.54 cr shares through an implied multiple written by AUROPHARMA.mult.js; (3) other income is built from gross cash (Aurobindo holds ~Rs8,800 cr of cash and ~Rs8,400 cr of debt at the same time), so treasuryYield is 0 and the build sits in `otherIncomeBuild`; interest is built from gross debt in `interestBuild`. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by business (businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY27E +16.7%, of which roughly 9pp is the weaker rupee (FY27E Rs94.5/US$ vs Rs88.3 in FY26; Europe Rs110/EUR vs ~Rs102.5) and ~5pp Lannett: US US$1,800mn (Q1 US$399mn; Q2-Q4 base US$390-410mn a quarter with ~10 launches a quarter offsetting price erosion, plus Lannett ~US$60-70mn a quarter from 29-Jun-2026 incl. gAdvair from Aug-2026); Europe EUR1,105mn (+10%: Q1 EUR267mn, +11% in constant currency, management guides double digits); Growth Markets US$460mn (+16%: Q1 US$113mn incl. the Khandelwal brands from Jan-2026); ARV US$140mn (Q1 US$35mn; tender business); APIs +10% (Q1 +14.6%; Pen-G/6-APA external sales). FY28E +9.8%: US US$1,940mn (base +2.5%, Lannett ~US$290mn full year), Europe EUR1,200mn (+8.5%), Growth Markets US$505mn, ARV US$135mn, APIs +8%, rupee Rs96.5/US$. FY29E +7.3%: US US$2,000mn, Europe EUR1,290mn, Growth Markets US$555mn, ARV US$130mn, APIs +7%, Rs98.5/US$. No biosimilar US revenue and no TheraNym (MSD) revenue before FY29 beyond what is inside Europe and Growth Markets.

businessLines._why: FY26 revenue by business (Q4FY26 presentation): US Rs14,408 cr (US$1,631mn), Europe Rs10,315 cr (EUR1,006mn), Growth Markets Rs3,499 cr (US$397mn), ARV Rs1,384 cr (US$157mn), APIs Rs4,047 cr = Rs33,653 cr. The rupee is assumed to weaken ~2% a year from the Q1FY27 average (Rs94.53/US$; Rs110/EUR on Europe's Rs2,937 cr / EUR267mn), the same US$ path as our Cipla and Zydus reports.

assumptions._marginWhy: Company EBITDA before forex and other income: 20.8% (FY25), 20.4% (FY26), 20.6% reported / 21.0% operating in Q1FY27 (before a Rs43 cr one-time lease-receivable write-off). Guidance: 'north of 21%' and EBITDA above Rs8,000 cr in FY27 (6-Aug-2026). FY27E 21.0% (Rs8,250 cr): Pen-G and 6-APA swing from a Rs200 cr+ EBITDA loss in FY26 to profit (PLI Rs240 cr per 10,000 t; minimum import price to Jan-2027), China from a ~US$7mn loss to positive, R&D down to Rs1,450-1,500 cr (4.7% -> 3.8% of revenue) as biosimilar phase-3 trials end; offset by the end of gRevlimid, US price erosion, Eugia remediation, Lannett integration (lower margin at first) and biosimilar launch costs. FY28E-29E 21.5%: Lannett synergies (SG&A, procurement, utilisation from ~40%), Europe above 20%, China scale; we stop short of ICICI Direct's 22.3% because Eugia's best plants cannot launch new products. Each 1pp of FY28E margin is ~Rs430 cr of EBITDA (~6% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Screener cash capex Rs3,562 / 2,520 / 3,105 cr in FY24-26 (FY26 net capex US$341mn, company). Q1FY27 net capex US$78mn. CFO (10-Feb-2026): no greenfield beyond biologics, capex not beyond ~US$150-200mn a year plus US$80-120mn for the biologics CMO over two years; TheraNym Unit 2 US$150-180mn from Oct-2026 to 2029; 10,000 L of new bioreactors at CuraTeQ. FY27E = US$300mn organic (~Rs2,835 cr) + Lannett US$247mn (Rs2,335 cr at Rs94.53, paid in Q1FY27; engine workaround, no acquisitions line) + A1 Biochem US$13.6mn (~Rs130 cr) = Rs5,300 cr (ICICI Direct models Rs5,325 cr). FY28E US$280mn (Rs2,700 cr); FY29E US$260mn (Rs2,550 cr), ~5.5% of revenue.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs1,778 cr = 6.6% of average gross block (Screener: Rs24,463 cr -> Rs29,251 cr); Q1FY27 Rs487 cr (Rs1,948 cr annualised) before Lannett. The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs5,214 cr) and depreciates capex at once, so we use 6.4%: FY27E ~Rs2,040 cr incl. Lannett's plant and acquired products.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: Aurobindo carries gross cash and gross debt side by side (Mar-26: Rs10,676 cr of cash and investments, Rs7,673 cr of debt; Jun-26: Rs8,790 cr and Rs8,393 cr), so a yield on the engine's small net cash would understate both income and interest. Treasury income is built on gross cash in otherIncomeBuild and interest on gross debt in interestBuild.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged (otherIncomeBuild; AUROPHARMA.ctx.js checks the build). FY26 company other income Rs492 cr (AR FY26 note 25): treasury Rs305 cr (bank-deposit interest Rs265 cr, other deposits Rs27 cr ex the lease receivable, debentures Rs7 cr, investments Rs3 cr, dividends Rs2 cr, gains Rs1 cr) = 3.2% of average company gross cash (Rs9,492 cr); interest on the East Windsor lease receivable Rs27 cr (ends: the receivable was derecognised in Q1FY27); write-backs Rs4 cr (one-off); miscellaneous Rs155 cr (not broken down; treated as recurring). FY27E = Q1 actual Rs212 cr + Q2-Q4 (3.2% x average gross cash, three quarters + miscellaneous Rs155 cr x 3/4). FY28E-29E = 3.2% x average gross cash + miscellaneous Rs160 / 165 cr. Gross cash = engine net cash + Rs154 cr (company vs Screener basis at Mar-26) + gross debt (interestBuild). Forex gains (Rs53 cr in Q1) are not forecast.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs384 cr; Q1FY27 Rs102 cr (average cost 4.8%, down from 5.0%). Built in interestBuild: average gross debt x 4.7% + ~Rs30 cr of lease interest; gross debt Rs7,673 cr (Mar-26), Rs8,393 cr (Jun-26, after Lannett), assumed Rs8,000 cr (Mar-27), Rs7,500 cr (Mar-28), Rs7,000 cr (Mar-29) as packing-credit and term loans are repaid from free cash flow.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective rate 31.5% in FY26 and 31.9% in Q1FY27, high because no deferred-tax credit is booked on losses of new subsidiaries (CuraTeQ, TheraNym, China); CFO guides 28-29% by FY27-end as those turn profitable. FY27E 30% (Q1 32%, then 29%), 28.5% and 28% after.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 interim dividend Rs4 a share (Rs232 cr, 6.6% of EPS). FY27E payout = Rs4.5 a share (~Rs260 cr) + the Rs800 cr buyback paid in Apr-May 2026 (engine workaround: no buyback line) = ~Rs1,060 cr, 23.5% of FY27E profit. FY28E-29E 6.5%, the historical dividend payout; buybacks (2024 and 2026) are opportunistic and not assumed.

dcf._betaWhy: 0.9 (cost of equity 11.9%): two-thirds of revenue from regulated generics where prices fall every year, plant-inspection risk (two Eugia warning letters), a possible US generics tariff from 2028 and a 7% promoter pledge; offset by a diversified, cash-generating base and ~zero net debt (so cost of equity ~ WACC).
dcf._tgWhy: 5%: US generics grow low single digits in dollars, Europe mid single digits, plus ~2% rupee depreciation; lower than our 5.5% for India-led Cipla.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 21.5% held: no new windfall; biosimilars and the MSD CMO could add upside after FY29 that we do not assume.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex settles at 5% of revenue (FY24-26 9-12% incl. Pen-G, China and biologics; maintenance ~4%); depreciation 4.5% of revenue (FY26 5.3%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: US base grows again (Eugia Unit III and Unit I cleared, Lannett respiratory launches and plant transfers work, US biosimilar filings land on time), Europe keeps double-digit growth, Pen-G and China earn full margins.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: US price erosion outruns launches, Eugia stays blocked, Lannett synergies slip, the Pen-G import floor lapses in Jan-2027 and a 2028 generics tariff looms.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Aurobindo: P/E on FY28E or 12-month-forward EPS (ICICI Direct 18x FY28E, Prabhudas Lilladher 18x FY28E, Motilal Oswal 20x 12-month forward). Our multiple: Aurobindo's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (no trough years on that basis), times the pharma sector factor (+5.45%, PLAYBOOK §7c), nearest half-turn; bull = 75th percentile x factor, bear = 25th percentile x factor. Applied to EPS per post-buyback share (57.54 cr shares); the engine carries it as an implied multiple of its own Sep-28E EPS (on the FY26 count of 58.09 cr), written by tools/authoring/AUROPHARMA.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Aurobindo's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (Screener) times the same sector factor, nearest half-turn, on trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus the engine's net cash at Sep-2027; bull/bear at the 75th/25th percentiles x factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.9% cost of equity (~WACC: net debt is ~zero), terminal growth 5%, plus the engine's net cash at Mar-27.

derivedPe._note: Derived P/E on EPS per post-buyback share (57.54 cr); pe.multiple is the same value restated on the engine EPS (58.09 cr shares).
